title: Enumeration of microparticles on a gridded filter using a stratified random sampling tool
author: Paterson, Silverstan, et al.

The total number of squares in each zone is shown in Panel F, and this counting program uses the 3:3:1 “no partial grid cells” scheme as the default for the stratified random sampling model. steps.title: Prepare sediment samples and filter
steps.instruction: Sieve each environmental sediment sample between 63 µm and 500 µm, then plate the particles onto a 47 mm diameter gridded filter (16 rows × 16 columns, 217 total grid cells; exclude partial edge cells to obtain 167 cells) using the vacuum‑filter apparatus described by Thaysen et al.

steps.title: Assign grid cell IDs in Excel VBA
steps.instruction: Create an Excel workbook with a Visual Basic® macro that numbers every grid cell (ID 1‑217) and stores the layout; the program utility will later accept particle counts per cell.

steps.title: Count particles per grid cell
steps.instruction: Under a stereomicroscope, identify tire‑road‑wear particles (TRWPs) in each cell using visual and physical attributes, record the count for each cell in the Excel VBA utility, and time the counting to assess labor.

steps.title: Generate heat maps and calculate CV
steps.instruction: Export the cell‑by‑cell counts, plot heat‑maps and particle‑density profiles for the filter, then compute the coefficient of variation (CV) for the whole filter and for each of the seven concentric strata using CV = (σ / ȳ) × 100. Report whole‑filter CV values (120 %–178 %).

steps.title: Define concentric strata on filter
steps.instruction: Divide the filter into seven concentric ring strata (1 = center to 7 = outer edge) as shown in Fig. 2; note that partial cells in strata 6 & 7 are counted as 0.5 cells. Record the average particle‑percentage per stratum: 4.0 % ± 1.2, 10.8 % ± 2.2, 24.0 % ± 5.8, 22.7 % ± 2.1, 21.1 % ± 4.0, 12.4 % ± 1.7, 5.1 % ± 2.7.

steps.title: Perform k‑means clustering in RStudio
steps.instruction: Open RStudio (Version 2022.12.0) and run k‑means clustering on the raw TRWP counts per cell. Use the average silhouette method to select the optimal number of clusters (k = 3). Record the resulting cluster assignments and define three strata (h1 = cells 1‑3, h2 = cells 4‑5, h3 = cells 6‑7) for the 3:2:2 scheme.

steps.title: Select stratification schemes
steps.instruction: Based on clustering and CV analysis, adopt two stratification arrangements: (a) 3:2:2 – h1 = 1‑3, h2 = 4‑5, h3 = 6‑7; (b) 3:3:1 – h1 = 1‑3, h2 = 4‑6, h3 = 7 (the latter chosen for further work).

steps.title: Calculate optimum sample allocation
steps.instruction: Apply Eq. (2) nh = Nhi σhi / ∑(Nh σh) to each stratum of both schemes, using the average standard deviations across the five samples. Convert the resulting nh values to percentages of total cells: for 3:3:1 → h1 30 %, h2 60 %, h3 10 %; for 3:2:2 → h1 30 %, h2 40 %, h3 30 %. Note that these allocations match proportional allocation based on particle abundance.

steps.title: Download and set up Excel sampling tool
steps.instruction: Clone the VBA counting tool from https://github.com/KayliPaterson/SamplingTool (Excel Macro extension version 2301, VBA 7.1). Open the workbook; the default layout (Fig. 6) includes zones C, M, E corresponding to the 3:3:1‑no‑partials scheme.

steps.title: Configure sampling parameters and generate random sample
steps.instruction: In the ‘Calculator’ tab, enter the desired number of cells to sample (e.g., 10, 30, 50, 80, 110) in the “Cells to Sample” box, select the stratification scheme (3:3:1‑no‑partials or 3:2:2), then click “Random Sample” (or “Sample All” to select every non‑partial cell). The macro runs a path‑finding algorithm that starts at the bottom‑left origin and lists the nearest next cell, reducing microscope stage travel.

substeps.instruction: Use the “Clear” button to remove a generated sample; “Clear Sample Info” clears all progress fields.
The “Save” button transfers the sampled cell IDs and any entered counts to the “Data” tab.

steps.title: Record counts and compute total particle estimate
steps.instruction: Enter TRWP counts (and optionally a second particle type) for each sampled cell in column G of the tool. The workbook then calculates the total filter count τ using Eq. (3) τ = ∑h τh and Eq. (4) τh = (Nh / nh) ∑i yhi, where yhi are the observed counts in stratum h.

steps.title: Run stochastic simulation to evaluate accuracy
steps.instruction: For each sample size (10, 30, 50, 80, 110 cells) and for both schemes with and without partial cells, run the random‑sampling macro 20 times. Compare each τ estimate to the known total count; report the percentage of trials within ±15 % of the true value and compute variance using Eq. (5) var(τ) = ∑h Nh(Nh − nh)σh² / nh.

steps.title: Report counting time and adjust sample size
steps.instruction: Document the average counting time (88 ± 21 min per filter, N = 5), which equals ~0.4 min per grid cell or 2.5 ± 0.6 TRWPs min⁻¹. Use this rate to estimate time savings (e.g., 80 cells ≈ 32 min, ~½ the full‑filter time) and decide on an appropriate sample size for future studies, especially if multiple particle types are to be enumerated.
